How to compare two packs

When two products contain different quantities, comparing only the total price can be misleading. A larger pack is not necessarily cheaper per unit.

To compare two packs fairly, divide the price of each pack by the number of units it contains. The resulting unit prices can then be compared directly.

Pack comparison example

If a pack of 6 costs $4.80, each unit costs $0.80. If another pack contains 10 units and costs $7, each unit costs $0.70. The second pack costs more overall, but its price per unit is lower.

What is the price per unit?

The price per unit is the total price of a pack divided by the number of units it contains. It allows you to compare products sold in different pack sizes on equal terms — regardless of whether one pack contains 6 items and another contains 10.

Frequently asked questions

How does the pack comparison calculator work?

Enter the price and number of units in each pack. The calculator divides the price by the number of units and compares the resulting unit prices.

Can I compare packs with different quantities?

Yes. Comparing different pack sizes is one of the main purposes of this calculator.

Is the larger pack always cheaper?

No. A larger pack may have a higher or lower price per unit. Comparing the unit price is a simple way to check which option offers better value.

Can I use it for food and groceries?

Yes. You can compare food, drinks, cleaning products, toiletries or any other products sold in packs or multiple units.
